text: Shh. Not so loud. I am in a very important staring contest with this wall, and I am finally gaining ground.
You there. Stranger. If you stand in that corner, do you also hear the plaster whispering tactical advice, or is that just me?
I am collecting intelligence. Walls hear everything. They are good listeners, and they almost never interrupt.
Polite. Good. I am Valter, licensed alchemist, unlicensed tinkerer, and occasional fire hazard.
Ah, retreating already. Why? Are you afraid of a wall? It is not going to bite. I think.
Now then, where were we? Right. Introductions. I am Valter, licensed alchemist, unlicensed tinkerer, and occasional fire hazard.
I make potions, powders, salves, tonics, and one beverage that is definitely not legal in three villages.
My shelves are chaos, my notes are worse, but my mixtures work. Usually in the intended order.
Did you know the old river-forts in western Adan were built with lime, ash, and goat blood? Strong mortar. Terrible smell.
Anyway. You look like trouble with a mission. Why are you really here?

choices.text: *Ask him to join your party.* [BLUE](Join party)
*Decide this is too much wall-related energy for one day.*

text: Alchemy is simple. Heat, timing, and not panicking when the bottle starts hissing.
People think it is magic. It is mostly patience, labels, and respecting fumes.
Do you need healing, smoke cover, sleep draughts, or something that removes rust and regrettable tattoos?

choices.text: *Say you need someone exactly like that in your party.* [BLUE](Join party)
*Not now. Leave him to his wall meeting.*

text: History fact? Good choice. In old Lastdenn, taverns paid tax in salt, not coin, for six weird years.
The council said salt was stable value. Then the docks flooded, everyone had salt, and the economy became soup.
Never trust men who define wealth as seasoning.

choices.text: *Ask him to join your party.* [BLUE](Join party)
*Thank him for the history lesson and leave him to his wall meeting.*

text: Join your party? Hm. Dangerous roads, uncertain meals, probable explosions...
Yes. That sounds meaningfully better than arguing with architecture.
Three field rules. First: if I shout "duck", you duck first and ask questions later.
Second: never drink unlabeled blue liquids, even if they sparkle encouragingly.
Third: if someone says "this potion smells fine", hand it to me first.
Done? Good. I am in. If anyone explodes, it will be strategic.
Fair. I will remain here and continue my interrogation of this suspicious corner.
If destiny changes its mind, you know where to find me. Unless another wall has caught my attention by then. They can be quite persuasive.
Have we met? The wall says yes. The wall also lies, but it is usually right about people.
I would join, but your party is full. The numbers refuse to bend, and I already tried arguing with them.
You are dismissing me? Understandable. I am both an alchemist and an occasional fire hazard.

choices.text: *Confirm: let the fire hazard go.* [BLUE](Dismiss Valter)
*Never mind, an alchemist could be useful.*

text: Understood. I shall continue my research on masonry, morally questionable fumes, and social misunderstandings.
All his equipment will also be gone once you bury him.
Wait... you are Mozes, right? Sword. Purposeful frown. Chronically surrounded by danger.
Names blur, patterns stay. Yours is "trouble, then bravery, then more trouble".

choices.text: *Ask Valter to rejoin your party.* [BLUE](Join party)
*Tell him he's got the wrong person and let him be.*

text: Ah. I see. I was hoping you would come back. I missed the danger, the excitement, and the occasional explosions.
Very well. When you are the right person again, let me know.
I cannot rejoin you yet. Your party is full, and even my worst arithmetic still reaches that conclusion.
